title: Measures to Reduce Singaporeans’ Sugar Intake
what_it_is: Measures to Reduce Singaporeans’ Sugar Intake

sections.label: Diabetes cases and SSB measures
sections.summary: Asked how many diabetes cases are diagnosed yearly and when SSB label and advertising measures start; estimated 19,000 diagnoses yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) for each year in the past five years, how many diabetes cases have been diagnosed; and (b) when will the measures to reduce Singaporeans' sugar intake from sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs), namely, mandatory front-of-pack labels and advertising prohibitions be implemented.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We estimate that 19,000 patients are diagnosed to have diabetes each year based on our administrative data.

sections.label: Mandatory SSB labels and advertising prohibitions
sections.summary: Ministry announced mandatory nutrition labels and advertising prohibitions for less healthy pre-packaged SSBs; details and timeline to come at Committee of Supply.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: With this in mind, the Ministry announced in October last year that we will introduce mandatory nutrition labels and advertising prohibitions for less healthy pre-packaged sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Details of the two measures, including the implementation timeline, will be shared in the upcoming Committee of Supply debate.

sections.label: Extending measures to freshly prepared drinks
sections.summary: Considering extending labelling and advertising measures to freshly prepared drinks, consulting stakeholders; such drinks are about a third of sugar intake from drinks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The third supplementary question is whether there are plans to implement this more extensively to all mainstream schools and even our institutes of higher learning (IHLs) in the canteens and cafes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: I do not have the exact breakdown of what are the contributing factors of diabetes with me now, but what I have is the information on the freshly prepared drinks, such as bubble teas, blended coffee and local "kopi" and "teh".

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: This forms about a third of Singaporeans' sugar intake from drinks and our data suggests that it is a growing source of sugar intake in Singaporeans' diet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: So, addressing this other source of sugar in our diet could help us to more effectively achieve our objective of helping Singaporeans reduce their overall sugar intake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We have received feedback to tackle freshly prepared drinks and we are currently considering whether to extend the labelling and advertising measures to freshly prepared drinks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We are in the process of consulting the relevant stakeholders, such as the food and beverage industry, on possible measures, and more details will be shared when ready.

sections.label: Sugar tax on carbonated beverages
sections.summary: Ministry is studying a sugar tax on carbonated beverages and will discuss it at the Committee of Supply debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry considered introducing sugar tax on carbonated beverages?

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We are studying that and we will discuss this at the Committee of Supply debate.
